course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Web App Development for Data Science (with Streamlit & FastAPI/Flask)
course.description: This course introduces students to web development techniques for Data Science applications using Streamlit and FastAPI. Students learn how to build interactive data dashboards and machine learning applications using Python, without requiring traditional frontend technologies. The course covers Streamlit fundamentals for data visualization and user interaction, as well as backend API development with FastAPI for data services and model deployment. By the end of the course, students will be able to design, integrate, and present complete data‑driven web applications.

clos.description: Explain the architecture and execution model of Streamlit applications for data‑driven web development.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lectures with guided explanation, live demonstrations, interactive discussion, and concept‑based examples on Streamlit architecture and execution model
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Written quizzes, midterm examination (theory), short answer questions, class participation

clos.description: Develop interactive data applications using Streamlit widgets, layouts, and visualization components.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Hands‑on laboratory practice, guided coding sessions, problem‑based learning, instructor‑led demonstrations
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Laboratory exercises, practical assignments, Streamlit mini project, practical component of midterm exam

clos.description: Apply Streamlit session state and caching techniques to optimize performance of data applications.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lectures with case studies, live coding demonstrations, problem‑solving activities related to performance optimization
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab assignments, practical tests, evaluation of optimized applications, final project implementation

clos.description: Design and implement RESTful APIs using FastAPI to support data services and machine learning applications.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Project‑based learning, laboratory practice, independent development, system integration tasks, supervised project guidance
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Practical assignments, final examination (practical), final project and presentation

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Data Science Web Development & Streamlit Overview
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the role of web applications in Data Science. LLO2: Describe the purpose and features of Streamlit for data-driven applications.

topics.title: Topic 2: Streamlit Architecture & Execution Model
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain Streamlit’s execution and rerun model. LLO2: Analyze how user interactions trigger script reruns in Streamlit.

topics.title: Topic 3: Displaying Text, Data, and Layouts in Streamlit
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Use Streamlit functions to display text, tables, and DataFrames. LLO2: Create structured layouts using columns, containers, and sidebars.

topics.title: Topic 4: Widgets and User Interaction Handling
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Implement input widgets to capture user interaction. LLO2: Develop interactive data applications using widget-driven logic.

topics.title: Topic 5: Data Visualization in Streamlit
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Generate data visualizations using Streamlit built-in charts. LLO2: Integrate external visualization libraries (e.g., Matplotlib, Plotly) into Streamlit apps.

topics.title: Topic 6: Forms and Session State Management
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply Streamlit forms to control user input and app execution. LLO2: Manage application state using st.session_state.

topics.title: Topic 7: File Upload and Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Implement file upload functionality in Streamlit applications. LLO2: Perform basic exploratory data analysis on user-uploaded datasets.

topics.title: Topic 8: Caching and Performance Optimization in Streamlit
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate between st.cache_data and st.cache_resource. LLO2: Optimize application performance using appropriate caching techniques.

topics.title: Topic 9: Introduction to APIs and FastAPI Framework
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain RESTful API concepts and their role in data applications. LLO2: Create basic API endpoints using FastAPI.

topics.title: Topic 10: FastAPI CRUD Operations and Request Handling
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Implement CRUD operations using FastAPI. LLO2: Handle HTTP requests and responses with path and query parameters.

topics.title: Topic 11: FastAPI with Databases and ORM Integration
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Connect FastAPI applications to a relational database. LLO2: Use ORM tools to perform database operations.

topics.title: Topic 12: API Security, Authentication, and Error Handling
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply basic authentication and authorization techniques in APIs. LLO2: Implement proper error handling and validation mechanisms.

topics.title: Topic 13: Machine Learning Models as REST APIs
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Deploy trained machine learning models using FastAPI. LLO2: Handle prediction requests and responses through REST APIs.

topics.title: Topic 14: Streamlit–FastAPI Integration and Project Development
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Integrate Streamlit frontend applications with FastAPI backend services. LLO2: Design and build a complete data-driven web application combining frontend and backend components.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
